sources.title: Organizing Instruction and Study to Improve Student Learning
sources.design: Practice guide with study reviews and panel judgment
sources.subject: Mathematics, science and content-heavy subjects
sources.limitations: Evidence levels differ by recommendation and do not define a universal schedule
sources.certainty: Moderate for spacing and example interleaving, strong for re-exposure quizzes, minimal for pre-questions

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques
sources.population: Learners across ages in reviewed studies
sources.subject: Multiple
sources.limitations: Only bibliographic page and abstract inspected; detailed utility ratings unverified

sources.title: Using Technology to Support Postsecondary Student Learning
sources.design: Practice guide; recommendation 4 synthesizes eight studies
sources.subject: Multiple
sources.risk_of_bias: WWC reports five studies without reservations, two with reservations, and one with comparisons in both groups
sources.directness: Direct for postsecondary feedback; indirect for school-age AI tutoring

sources.title: Universal Design for Learning Guidelines version 3.0
sources.subject: Multiple
sources.intervention: Options for engagement, representation, action and expression
sources.outcomes: Access-oriented design considerations; no causal estimate
sources.limitations: Framework guidance does not establish that each adaptation improves measured learning

sources.title: Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence
sources.population: Children and adults in reviewed studies
sources.subject: Multiple
sources.limitations: Abstract inspected; not every possible matching hypothesis tested
sources.risk_of_bias: Few studies could test the hypothesis adequately
sources.consistency: Adequate supportive crossover evidence not found

sources.title: Is it really a neuromyth? A meta-analysis of the learning styles matching hypothesis
sources.subject: Varied
sources.outcomes: Average matching benefit and crossover evidence
sources.limitations: Only 26% of outcome measures supported crossover for at least two styles; low study quality
sources.certainty: Insufficient for widespread adoption despite positive pooled average

sources.title: Undesirable Difficulty Effects in the Learning of High-Element Interactivity Materials
sources.subject: High-element-interactivity tasks
sources.comparator: Worked examples followed by early problem solving
sources.limitations: Specific complex tasks; not a general rejection of retrieval practice

sources.title: Making AI Tutoring Productive: Evidence from a Mastery-Based Math Practice Experiment
sources.subject: Two mathematics topics
sources.intervention: AI support crossed with mastery progression
sources.comparator: Computer-assisted learning alone and non-mastery progression
sources.limitations: Delayed gains marginal and concentrated on practiced material; mastery alone did not improve delayed learning
sources.risk_of_bias: Randomization reported; full paper not independently appraised

sources.title: Examining the benefits of spaced retrieval practice on transfer and the student experience in the classroom
sources.subject: Course content
sources.limitations: No overall transfer effect; exploratory measures showed positive and negative transfer
sources.directness: Direct for repeated versus novel question distinction

sources.title: Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing
sources.design: Professional standards jointly published by AERA, APA and NCME
sources.subject: Multiple
sources.intervention: Validity, reliability and fairness requirements for intended score uses
sources.outcomes: Testing quality criteria, not an intervention outcome
sources.limitations: Standards do not supply psychometric coefficients for a newly drafted test
sources.certainty: Authoritative professional standards, not causal evidence

sources.title: A Brief Introduction to Evidence-Centered Design
sources.subject: Multiple
sources.intervention: Design claims, observable evidence and tasks together
sources.limitations: Only abstract and bibliographic page inspected; not causal evidence

sources.title: Formative assessment and elementary school student academic achievement: A review of the evidence
sources.design: Evidence review using WWC-style study screening
sources.subject: Mathematics, reading and writing
sources.comparator: No formative intervention or different practice
sources.limitations: Effects vary by subject and who directs assessment; self-directed writing evidence was insufficient
sources.risk_of_bias: 23 of 76 relevant studies met the review's causal confidence threshold
sources.directness: Direct for elementary formative assessment; indirect for other ages

sources.title: Knowledge tracing: Modeling the acquisition of procedural knowledge
sources.subject: Procedural skills
sources.intervention: Probabilistic estimate of latent skill acquisition from task history
sources.limitations: A model estimate depends on calibrated assumptions and observed task context
sources.directness: Direct for model existence; indirect for any new deployment
sources.certainty: Method reference, not evidence of universal effectiveness

sources.title: Knowledge Tracing Over Time: A Longitudinal Analysis
sources.subject: Platform content
sources.intervention: BKT model variants evaluated over time
sources.limitations: Predictive performance is not proof of a learning intervention effect
sources.risk_of_bias: Dataset and evaluation details need full appraisal
sources.consistency: Reported performance varies with population and time

sources.title: Leveraging the Potential of Learning Analytics in Higher Education Requires Inclusive Policies and Practices
sources.subject: Multiple
sources.intervention: Equity, transparency and learner agency in data governance
sources.outcomes: Ethical design considerations; no causal learning outcome
sources.limitations: Higher-education framing does not settle child-data rules or local law
sources.directness: Direct for analytics governance, indirect for minors

rules.rationale: Retrieving taught material can support later recall; complex new material may first need worked examples.
rules.scope: Content requiring durable recall after initial instruction
rules.conditions: Use answer-free attempts and correction; separate repeated-item recall from novel transfer.
rules.counterexamples: Early complex novice problem solving may cause unproductive difficulty.
rules.contraindications: Do not infer low ability from a failed first attempt.
rules.uncertainty: Optimal form and transfer depend on knowledge and domain.
rules.evaluation_method: Compare delayed unassisted recall and novel transfer with a comparable baseline.

rules.rationale: Return to important content after a delay when the course does not already provide cumulative reuse.
rules.scope: Knowledge intended to persist beyond immediate instruction
rules.conditions: Choose feasible review intervals from retention target, learner response and calendar.
rules.counterexamples: Routine daily use may already supply spaced exposure.
rules.contraindications: Do not claim a universal fixed schedule or promise unsupported reminders.
rules.uncertainty: Best interval for each learner and subject remains unknown.
rules.evaluation_method: Measure delayed unassisted performance against a comparable study pattern.

rules.rationale: Alternate worked solutions and practice, then reduce support as prior knowledge develops.
rules.conditions: Check prior knowledge and interacting task steps.
rules.counterexamples: Experienced learners may find worked steps redundant.
rules.contraindications: Do not force a procedural example pattern onto interpretive tasks.
rules.evaluation_method: Compare later independent performance across support levels.

rules.rationale: Specific correction after an attempt helps identify and address errors.
rules.conditions: Connect feedback to observed response and objective; permit retry.
rules.counterexamples: Multiple defensible interpretations require criterion-based discussion.
rules.contraindications: Do not diagnose a misconception from one response.
rules.uncertainty: Timing and granularity depend on task and stakes.
rules.evaluation_method: Inspect later independent attempts on equivalent tasks.

rules.rationale: Offer appropriate ways to access, engage with and express knowledge while retaining the target construct.
rules.conditions: Identify the construct before choosing representation or accommodation.
rules.counterexamples: Audio changes the construct of a reading-fluency assessment.
rules.contraindications: Do not infer disability from labels or claim compliance without checking.
rules.uncertainty: Each adaptation has no implied causal effect.
rules.evaluation_method: Check access with intended users and relevant assistive technology; assess learning separately.

rules.rationale: Supported correct responses and later independent recall or transfer are distinct observations.
rules.scope: AI tutoring, assisted practice and analytics
rules.conditions: Record hints and solutions, then probe independently after a delay where feasible.
rules.counterexamples: Higher practice accuracy can accompany slower progress and little delayed transfer.
rules.contraindications: Do not turn immediate scores or an arbitrary mastery threshold into a forecast.
rules.uncertainty: LLM tutoring evidence is emerging and context-specific.
rules.evaluation_method: Compare assisted practice, delayed unassisted results and novel items separately.

rules.rationale: A positive mean matching effect does not establish a dependable crossover for each purported learning style.
rules.conditions: Choose modes for content, access and learner preference without fixed VARK types.
rules.counterexamples: Individual preferences can be accommodated without claiming matching improves learning.
rules.contraindications: Do not prescribe from a fixed learning-style label.
rules.evaluation_method: Require sound crossover outcome studies before proposing a general matching rule.

rules.rationale: Interpret scores only for the construct and intended use supported by evidence; design tasks to elicit relevant observations.
rules.scope: Assessment blueprints, scored items and readiness reports
rules.conditions: Name the claim, evidence, task and scoring interpretation; check fairness, precision and alternate valid answers.
rules.counterexamples: One original mock examination without calibration cannot provide a standardized ability estimate.
rules.contraindications: Do not invent reliability, validity or norming coefficients.
rules.uncertainty: High-stakes use needs qualified human and local examination review.
rules.evaluation_method: Audit objectives, item evidence, solutions, scoring and intended score-use argument.

rules.rationale: Formative evidence can guide timely changes to instruction, with effects varying across subject and implementation.
rules.conditions: Collect evidence targeted to a decision and use more than one probe when the cause of an error is uncertain.
rules.counterexamples: A single wrong answer may reflect language, execution or conceptual difficulty.
rules.contraindications: Do not claim a formative item has standardized diagnostic precision without validation.
rules.uncertainty: School-age and postsecondary evidence differ; writing evidence was less conclusive.
rules.evaluation_method: Check whether an informed instructional change improves later independent objective-aligned performance.

rules.rationale: Sparse and assisted events support descriptive reports, while fitted mastery models need enough valid data and drift checks.
rules.conditions: Report numerator, denominator, time window, assistance and missingness; validate any predictive model on the target population.
rules.counterexamples: A model may predict immediate answers while failing to explain delayed unassisted learning.
rules.contraindications: Do not assign calibrated mastery probabilities from a few events or infer causation from correlations.
rules.uncertainty: Knowledge-tracing assumptions and population shift can change predictions.
rules.evaluation_method: Compare prediction calibration and delayed independent outcomes on held-out learners and later cohorts.

rules.rationale: Learning analytics requires purpose-limited, transparent handling with learner agency and access considerations.
rules.scope: Learner event collection and project reporting
rules.conditions: Use authorized minimal data, disclose audience and purpose, and check local requirements for minors.
rules.counterexamples: A small group can be identifiable even when names are removed.
rules.contraindications: Do not place private learner records in public shared skill artifacts.
rules.uncertainty: Jurisdiction-specific privacy requirements are outside these sources and need separate verification.
rules.evaluation_method: Audit collection, access, export/deletion path and disclosure risk for the intended population.
